content: 1. Tetracycline and Axitinib: Tetracycline increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, closely monitor the patient and reduce the axitinib dose as necessary. 2. Metronidazole and Axitinib: Metronidazole increases the levels of axitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor closely and adjust the axitinib dose as needed. 3. Metronidazole and Balsalazide: Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely. 4. Tetracycline and Balsalazide: Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely. 5. Tetracycline and Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitor closely. 6. Metronidazole and Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitor closely. 7. Tetracycline and BCG Vaccine (Live): Tetracycline decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic treatment is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 8. Metronidazole and BCG Vaccine (Live): Metronidazole decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic treatment is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 9. Tetracycline and Bemiparin: Tetracycline increases the effects of bemiparin through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 10. Bismuth Subsalicylate and Benazepril: Bismuth subsalicylate decreases the effects of benazepril through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Salicylates may also increase the nephrotoxic effects of ACE inhibitors. 11. Metronidazole and Biotin: Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely. 12. Tetracycline and Biotin: Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely. 13. Bismuth Subsalicylate and Tetracycline: Bismuth subsalicylate decreases the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Tetracycline and Brexpiprazole: Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. 15. Metronidazole and Brexpiprazole: Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust the brexpiprazole dose as needed. 16. Tetracycline and Buprenorphine (Subdermal Implant): Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine (subdermal implant) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should be transitioned to a buprenorphine dosage form that allows dose adjustments. 17. Metronidazole and Buprenorphine (Long-Acting Injection): Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine (long-acting injection) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor plasma levels to ensure adequate buprenorphine levels. 18. Tetracycline and Calcium Salts (e.g., Calcium Acetate, Carbonate, Chloride, Citrate, Gluconate): Either agent decreases the levels of the other by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. 19. Metronidazole and Cannabidiol: Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 20. Tetracycline and Cannabidiol: Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust the cannabidiol dose as needed. 21. Metronidazole and Capivasertib: Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the capivasertib dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 22. Tetracycline and Capivasertib: Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust the capivasertib dose as needed. 23. Metronidazole and Carbamazepine: Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 24. Tetracycline and Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of tetracycline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Tetracycline and Cholera Vaccine: Tetracycline decreases the effects of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may be active against the vaccine strain. 26. Metronidazole and Cholera Vaccine: Metronidazole decreases the effects of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may be active against the vaccine strain. 27. Metronidazole and Cilostazol: Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Tetracycline and Cobicistat: Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If short-term use of moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the cobicistat dose.
